facts: The central angle $\theta$ in radians is the ratio of arc length $l$ to radius $r$: $\theta = \dfrac{l}{r}$.
Because radian measure is a ratio of two lengths, it is a **dimensionless** quantity.
One full revolution of $360^{\circ}$ equals $2\pi\text{ radians}$, since $\theta = \dfrac{2\pi r}{r} = 2\pi$.
A straight angle of $180^{\circ}$ equals $\pi\text{ radians} \approx 3.14159\text{ radians}$.
An angle of $\theta\text{ radians}$ subtends an arc containing $\theta$ radius lengths: $l = r\theta$.
The fraction of a circle represented by angle $\theta$ is $\dfrac{\theta}{2\pi}$.

foundation.question_text: State the geometric definition of $1\text{ radian}$ in terms of the radius $r$ and the subtended arc length $l$.
foundation.solution_text: One radian is the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the radius ($l = r$).

foundation.question_text:
An arc of length $12\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle $\theta$ at the centre of a circle of radius $4\text{ cm}$.
Find the angle $\theta$ in radians.

A sector of a circle of radius $5\text{ cm}$ has an arc length of $15\text{ cm}$.
Find the angle $\theta$ subtended at the centre in radians.

development.solution_text:
By definition, when the arc length equals the radius ($l = r$), the central angle is $1\text{ radian}$.
$\theta = \dfrac{l}{r} = \dfrac{r}{r} = 1\text{ radian}$
